H3999:
1) flood, deluge.
1a) Noah's flood that submerged the entire planet earth under water for about a year
++++
Some think Noah's flood was only local. However the description of it found in Gen. 6 through 8 makes this patently absurd. If it was local, Noah had 120 years to migrate out of the area to safe ground! Why waste all that effort building a ship? He only had to move less than 1500 feet a day to reach the farthest point on the globe! With the possible exception of Ps 29:10, this word always refers to Noah's flood. The real reason for insisting on a local flood is the acceptance of evolution with its long geological ages. Most holding that view are not willing to allow a global world wide flood to have happened less than 5000 years ago. To admit such eliminates the need for the geological ages for most of the geological column would have been rapidly laid down by Noah's flood.

When the female of the scarlet worm species was ready to give birth to her young, she would attach her body to the trunk of a tree, fixing herself so firmly and permanently that she would never leave again. The eggs deposited beneath her body were thus protected until the larvae were hatched and able to enter their own life cycle. As the mother died, the crimson fluid stained her body and the surrounding wood. From the dead bodies of such female scarlet worms, the commercial scarlet dyes of antiquity were extracted. What a picture this gives of Christ, dying on the tree, shedding His precious blood that He might |bring many sons unto glory| (Heb 2:10)! He died for us, that we might live through him! Ps 22:6 describes such a worm and gives us this picture of Christ. (cf. Isa 1:18) (from page 73, |Biblical Basis for Modern Science|, 1985, Baker Book House, by Henry Morris)

H4327:
1) kind, sometimes a species (usually of animals)
++++
Groups of living organisms belong in the same created |kind| if they have descended from the same ancestral gene pool. This does not preclude new species because this represents a partitioning of the original gene pool. Information is lost or conserved not gained. A new species could arise when a population is isolated and inbreeding occurs. By this definition a new species is not a new |kind| but a further partitioning of an existing |kind|.

G5532: From the base of chraomai or chre; employment, i.e. An affair; also occasion, demand, requirement or destitution.
G4241: It becomes, is fitting to, is right. Apparently a primary verb; to tower up, i.e. to be suitable or proper.
G305: To go up, mount, ascend; of things: I rise, spring up, come up. From ana and the base of basis; to go up.
G2106: To be well-pleased, think it good, be resolved. From eu and dokeo; to think well of, i.e. Approve; specially, to approbate.
G321: From ana and ago; to lead up; by extension to bring out; specially, to sail away.
G3522: To fast, abstain from food. From nestis; to abstain from food.
G3983: To be hungry, needy, desire earnestly. From the same as penes; to famish; figuratively, to crave.
G4334: From pros and erchomai; to approach, i.e. come near, visit, or worship, assent to.
G4419: An extremity, battlement, parapet, apex. Neuter of a presumed derivative of pterux; a winglet, i.e. extremity.
G1781: To give orders (injunctions, instructions, commands). From en and the base of telos; to enjoin.
G4350: From pros and kopto; to strike at, i.e. Surge against; specially, to stub on, i.e. Trip up.
G1598: To put to the test, make trial of, tempt, try. From ek and peirazo; to test thoroughly.
G2889: Probably from the base of komizo; orderly arrangement, i.e. Decoration; by implication, the world (morally).
G4567: An adversary, Satan. Of Chaldee origin corresponding to ma'bad; the accuser, i.e. The devil.
G3000: To serve, especially God, perhaps simply: I worship. From latris; to minister, i.e. Render religious homage.
G3864: By the sea. From para and thalassa; along the sea, i.e. Maritime.
G2521: To sit, be seated, enthroned; I dwell, reside. From kata; and hemai; to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside.
G393: To make to rise, I rise, shine (generally of the sun, and hence met.). From ana and the base of telos; to arise.
G4043: From peri and pateo; to tread all around, i.e. Walk at large; figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow.
G293: Prop: something thrown around; a fishing-net, drag-net. From a compound of the base of amphoteros and ballo; a net.
G1205: Come hither, come, hither, an exclamatory word. From deuro and an imperative form of eimi; come hither!
G4260: To go forward, advance. From pro and the base of basis; to walk forward, i.e. Advance.
G2199: Zebedee, father of the apostles James and John. Of Hebrew origin; Zebedaeus, an Israelite.
G2675: From kata and a derivative of artios; to complete thoroughly, i.e. Repair or adjust.
G4013: To lead or carry about (or around), go about, traverse. From peri and ago; to take around; reflexively, to walk around.
G4864: From sunago; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish |synagogue|; by analogy, a Christian church.
G4947: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia. Probably of Hebrew origin; Syria, a region of Asia.
G4912: From sun and echo; to hold together, i.e. To compress or arrest; figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy.
G931: Torture, torment, examination by torture. Perhaps remotely from the same as basis; a touch-stone, i.e. torture.
G1139: To be possessed, be under the power of an evil-spirit or demon. Middle voice from daimon; to be exercised by a d?Mon.
G4583: To be a lunatic, be moonstruck, epileptic.
G3885: Afflicted with paralysis. From a derivative of paraluo; as if dissolved, i.e. |paralytic|.
G3793: From a derivative of echo; a throng; by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot.
G1179: From deka and polis; the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria.
G2816: To inherit, obtain (possess) by inheritance, acquire. From kleronomos; to be an heir to.
G1372: To thirst for, desire earnestly. From a variation of dipsos; to thirst for.
G5526: To feed, satisfy, fatten. From chortos; to fodder, i.e. to gorge.
G1655: Full of pity, merciful, compassionate. From eleeo; compassionate.
G1518: Pacific, loving peace, a peace-maker. From eirenopoios and poieo; pacificatory, i.e. peaceable.
G1377: To pursue, hence: I persecute. A prolonged form of a primary verb dio; to pursue; by implication, to persecute.
G3679: To reproach, revile, upbraid. From oneidos; to defame, i.e. Rail at, chide, taunt.
G21: To exult, be full of joy. From agan and hallomai; properly, to jump for joy, i.e. Exult.
G3408: (a) pay, wages, salary, (b) reward, recompense, punishment. Apparently a primary word; pay for service, good or bad.
G3471: From moros; to become insipid; figuratively, to make as a simpleton.
G2480: To have strength, be strong, be in full health and vigor, be able; meton: I prevail. From ischus; to have force.
G2662: From kata and pateo; to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain.
G2545: To ignite, light, burn, lit. and met; I consume with fire. Apparently a primary verb; to set on fire, i.e. Kindle or consume.
G3426: A dry measure, nearly two English gallons. Of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. Certain measure for things dry.
G2989: To shine, give light. A primary verb; to beam, i.e. Radiate brilliancy.
G3543: From nomos; properly, to do by law, i.e. To accustom; by extension, to deem or regard.
G2647: From kata and luo; to loosen down, i.e. to demolish; specially to halt for the night.
G3928: From para and erchomai; to come near or aside, i.e. To approach, go by, perish or neglect, avert.
G2503: Of Hebrew origin; |iota|, the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put for a very small part of anything.
G2762: Feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of keras; something horn-like, i.e. the apex of a Hebrew letter.
G4052: From perissos; to superabound, be in excess, be superfluous; also to cause to superabound or excel.
G4119: Or neuter pleion, or pleon comparative of polus; more in quantity, number, or quality; also the major portion.
G1777: Involved in, held in, hence: liable, generally with dat. (or gen.) of the punishment. From enecho; liable to.
G3710: To irritate, provoke, be angry. From orge; to provoke or enrage, i.e. become exasperated.
G4469: Empty, foolish. Of Chaldee origin; O empty one, i.e. Thou worthless.
G3474: Probably from the base of musterion; dull or stupid, i.e. Heedless, blockhead, absurd.
G1067: Of Hebrew origin; valley of Hinnom; ge-henna, a valley of Jerusalem, used as a name for the place of everlasting punishment.
G3403: To remember, call to mind, recall, mention. A prolonged form of mnaomai; to remind, i.e. to recall to mind.
G1259: From dia and allasso; to change thoroughly, i.e. to conciliate.
G2132: To be favorable, be kindly-disposed. From a compound of eu and nous; to be well- minded, i.e. Reconcile.
G3755: Until. For the genitive case of hostis; during which same time, i.e. Whilst.
G5438: From phulasso; a guarding or, the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or, the time, literally or figuratively.
G2835: Of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. The fourth part of an as.
G3431: To commit adultery (of a man with a married woman, but also of a married man). From moichos; to commit adultery.
G1937: To long for, covet, lust after, set the heart upon. From epi and thumos; to set the heart upon, i.e. Long for.
G4624: From skandalon; to entrap, i.e. Trip up (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure).
G1807: From ek and haireomai; actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release.
G4851: From sun and phero; to bear together, i.e. to collect, or to conduce; especially advantage.
G4983: Body, flesh; the body of the Church. From sozo; the body, used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively.
G647: Neuter of a adjective from a derivative of aphistemi; properly, something separative, i.e. divorce.
G4202: Fornication, whoredom; met: idolatry. From porneuo; harlotry; figuratively, idolatry.
G3429: To commit adultery, not only of a married woman but of a married man. From moichos; to commit adultery.
G1964: To take an oath, swear falsely. From epiorkos; to commit perjury.
G5286: A footstool. Neuter of a compound of hupo and pous; something under the feet, i.e. A foot-rest.
G4053: From peri; superabundant or superior; by implication, excessive; adverbially violently; neuter preeminence.
G4474: To slap, strike, smite with the hand. From a derivative of a primary rhepo; to slap.
G4600: The jawbone, cheek, jaw. Of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. the cheek or side of the face.
G4762: Strengthened from the base of trope; to twist, i.e. Turn quite around or reverse.
G29: Of foreign origin; properly, to be a courier, i.e. to press into public service.
G3400: A Roman mile, measuring 1478.5 meters or 5820.9 feet. Of Latin origin; a thousand paces, i.e. A |mile|.
G654: To turn away, pervert, remove; I restore, replace; mid: I desert, reject. From apo and strepho; to turn away or back.
G1155: To lend; mid: I borrow. From daneion; to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow.
G2190: Hated, hostile; subst: an enemy. From a primary echtho; hateful; usually as a noun, an adversary.
G782: To greet, salute, pay my respects to, welcome. To enfold in the arms, i.e. to salute, to welcome.
G1482: Pagan, heathen, gentile; subst: a Gentile, non-Jew. From ethnos; national, i.e. a Gentile.
G3770: In heaven, belonging to heaven, heavenly, from heaven. From ouranos; celestial, i.e. Belonging to or coming from the sky.
G1654: Abstr: alms-giving, charity; concr: alms, charity. From eleos; compassionateness, i.e. beneficence, or a benefaction.
G4537: To sound a trumpet. From salpigx; to trumpet, i.e. Sound a blast.
G4505: A narrow street or lane in a town or city. Prolongation from rhoumai in its original sense; an alley or avenue.
G568: To have in full, be far, it is enough. From apo and echo; to have out, i.e. Receive in full; to keep away, i.e. Be distant.
G710: On the left hand. Apparently a comparative of the same as ariston; the left hand.
G4113: A street, public square, broad way. Feminine of platus; a wide |plat| or |place|, i.e. Open square.
G945: To chatter, be long-winded, utter empty words, stammer, repeat. From Battos and logos; to stutter, i.e. to prate tediously.
G4180: Much-speaking, loquacity. From a compound of polus and logos; loquacity, i.e. Prolixity.
G1522: To hear, listen to, heed. From eis and akouo; to listen to.
G3666: To make like, liken; I compare. From homoios; to assimilate, i.e. Compare; passively, to become similar.
G37: From hagios; to make holy, i.e. purify or consecrate; to venerate.
G2307: An act of will, will; plur: wishes, desires. From the prolonged form of ethelo; a determination, i.e. choice or inclination.
G3783: A debt, offense, sin. From opheilo; something owed, i.e. a due; morally, a fault.
G3781: From opheilo; an ower, i.e. Person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor.
G1533: To lead into, bring in, announce. From eis and phero; to carry inward.
G3986: From peirazo; a putting to proof (of good), experience (of evil), solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication, adversity.
G3900: A falling away, lapse, slip, false step, trespass, sin. From parapipto; a side-slip, i.e. error or transgression.
G4659: From skuthros and a derivative of optanomai; angry-visaged, i.e. Gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance.
G853: From aphanes; to render unapparent, i.e. consume, or disappear.
G218: To anoint: festivally, in homage, medicinally, or in anointing the dead. To oil.
G1035: (a) abstr: eating, (b) food, a meal, (c) rust. From the base of bibrosko; eating; by extension food.
G1358: To dig through, break through. From dia and orusso; to penetrate burglariously.
G573: Single, simple, sound, perfect. Probably from a and the base of pleko; properly, folded together, i.e. Single.
G5460: Bright, luminous, full of light. From phos; lustrous, i.e. Transparent or well-illuminated.
G4214: How much, how great, how many. From an absolute pos and hos; interrogative pronoun how much (plural) many).
G472: From anti and the middle voice of echo; to hold oneself opposite to, i.e. adhere to; by extension to care for.
G3126: (Aramaic), riches, money, possessions, property. Of Chaldee origin; mammonas, i.e. Avarice.
G3514: To spin. From neo; to spin.
G1689: From en and blepo; to look on, i.e. to observe fixedly, or to discern clearly.
G1308: From dia and phero; to bear through, i.e. transport; usually to bear apart, i.e. to toss about; subjectively, to |differ|, or surpass.
G4369: To place (put) to, add; I do again. From pros and tithemi; to place additionally, i.e. Lay beside, annex, repeat.
G2648: To understand, take in a fact about, consider carefully. From kata and manthano; to learn thoroughly, i.e. to note carefully.
G2918: A lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the whole lily, the sword lily. Perhaps a prim word; a lily.
G837: (a) I cause to increase, become greater (b) I increase, grow. A prolonged form of a primary verb; to grow, i.e. Enlarge.
G294: To put on, clothe. From the base of amphoteros and hennumi; to enrobe.
G5528: Grass, herbage, growing grain, hay. Apparently a primary word; a |court| or |garden|, i.e. herbage or vegetation.
G2823: An oven, furnace. Of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in.
G3640: Of little faith. From oligos and pistis; incredulous, i.e. Lacking confidence.
G1934: To seek after, desire, search for, make inquiries about. From epi and zeteo; to search for; intensively, to demand, to crave.
G5535: To need, have need of, want, desire. From chreia; to make necessity, i.e. Be in want of.
G3358: An apparently primary word; a measure, literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion.
G3354: To measure (out), estimate. From metron; to measure; by implication, to admeasure.
G2657: To take note of, perceive, consider carefully, discern, detect, make account of. From kata and noieo; to observe fully.
G1544: To throw (cast, put) out; I banish; I bring forth, produce. From ek and ballo; to eject.
G1227: To see through, see clearly. From dia and blepo; to look through, i.e. Recover full vision.
G4486: To rend, break asunder; I break forth (into speech); I throw or dash down.
G2925: To knock, beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance. Apparently a primary verb; to rap.
G1929: (a) trans: I hand in, give up, (b) intrans: I give way (to the wind). From epi and didomi; to give over.
G3789: Probably from optanomai; a snake, figuratively, an artful malicious person, especially Satan.
G4116: Broad, wide; subst: a street. From plasso; spread out |flat|, i.e. Broad.
G684: Destruction, ruin, loss, perishing; eternal ruin. From a presumed derivative of apollumi; ruin or loss.
G2346: (a) I make narrow (strictly: by pressure); I press upon, (b) I persecute, press hard. Akin to the base of tribos; to crowd.
G5578: From pseudes and prophetes; a spurious prophet, i.e. Pretended foreteller or religious impostor.
G4263: A sheep. Probably neuter of a presumed derivative of probaino; something that walks forward, i.e., a sheep.
G3074: A wolf, of perhaps a jackal; often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities. Perhaps akin to the base of leukos; a wolf.
G1921: From epi and ginosko; to know upon some mark, i.e. Recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge.
G4816: To collect, gather. From sun and lego in its original sense; to collect.
G4718: A grape, cluster of grapes. Probably from the base of stephanos; a cluster of grapes.
G4395: From prophetes; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office.
G1140: An evil-spirit, demon; a heathen deity. Neuter of a derivative of daimon; a d?Monic being; by extension a deity.
G3670: From a compound of the base of homou and logos; to assent, i.e. Covenant, acknowledge.
G672: To go away, depart, withdraw. From apo and choreo; to go away.
G458: Lawlessness, iniquity, disobedience, sin. From anomos; illegality, i.e. Violation of law or wickedness.
G5429: Intelligent, prudent, sensible, wise. From phren; thoughtful, i.e. Sagacious or discreet; in a bad sense conceited.
G4363: From pros and pipto; to fall towards, i.e. prostrate oneself, or to rush upon.
G2311: To found, lay the foundation (lit. and met.). From themelios; to lay a basis for, i.e. erect, or consolidate.
G5055: (a) I end, finish, (b) I fulfill, accomplish, (c) I pay. From telos; to end, i.e. Complete, execute, conclude, discharge.
G1605: To strike with panic or shock; I amaze, astonish. From ek and plesso; to strike with astonishment.
G3142: Neuter of a presumed derivative of martus; something evidential, i.e. evidence given or, the Decalogue.
G1543: A centurion of the Roman army. Or hekatontarchos hek-at-on'-tar-khos; from hekaton and archo; the captain of one hundred men.
G2390: To heal, generally of the physical, sometimes of spiritual, disease. Middle voice of apparently a primary verb; to cure.
G4757: A soldier. From a presumed derivative of the same as stratia; a camper-out, i.e. A warrior.
G1683: Genitive case compound of emou and autos; of myself so likewise the dative case emautoi em-ow-to', and accusative case emauton em-ow-ton'.
G2296: (a) intrans: I wonder, marvel, (b) trans: I wonder at, admire. From thauma; to wonder; by implication, to admire.
G5118: So great, so large, so long, so many. From tosos and houtos; so vast as this, i.e. Such.
G2240: To have come, be present, have arrived. A primary verb; to arrive, i.e. Be present.
G347: To lay upon, lean against, lay down, make to recline; pass: I lie back, recline. From ana and klino; to lean back.
G4445: To be sick with a fever. From pura; to be on fire, i.e., to have a fever.
G2753: To command, order, direct, bid. From a primary kello; |hail|; to incite by word, i.e. Order.
G258: A fox; a fox-like, crafty person. Of uncertain derivation; a fox, i.e. a cunning person.
G2010: To turn to, commit, entrust; I allow, yield, permit. From epi and the base of trope; to turn over, i.e. Allow.
G1684: To step in; I go onboard a ship, embark. From en and the base of basis; to walk on, i.e. Embark, reach.
G4578: A shaking (as an earthquake); a storm. From seio; a commotion, i.e. a gale, an earthquake.
G2008: From epi and timao; to tax upon, i.e. Censure or admonish; by implication, forbid.
G1055: A calm. Of uncertain derivation; tranquillity.
G4217: Of what kind, of what manner. Apparently from pote and the base of pou; interrogatively, whatever, i.e. Of what possible sort.
G5219: From hupo and akouo; to hear under, i.e. To listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority.
G1046: From Gadara; a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara.
G5221: To meet, go to meet. From hupo and a derivative of anti; to go opposite under, i.e. To encounter, fall in with.
G5467: Perhaps from chalao through the idea of reducing the strength; difficult, i.e. Dangerous, or furious.
G2896: To cry aloud, shriek. A primary verb; properly, to |croak| or scream, i.e. to call aloud.
G2540: Fitting season, season, opportunity, occasion, time. Of uncertain affinity; an occasion, i.e. Set or proper time.
G3112: At a distance, far away, remote, alien. Feminine accusative case singular of makros; at a distance.
G1006: To feed, pasture. A prolonged form of a primary verb; to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze.
G1142: An evil-spirit, demon. From daio; a d?Mon or supernatural spirit.
G3729: To rush, hasten on. From horme; to start, spur or urge on, i.e. to dash or plunge.
G2911: A crag, precipice, steep bank. From kremannumi; overhanging, i.e. A precipice.
G1276: To cross over, pass over. From dia and a derivative of the base of peran; to cross entirely.
G2825: A couch, bed, portable bed or mat, a couch for reclining at meals, possibly also a bier. From klino; a couch.
G2293: To be of good courage, good cheer, be bold. From tharsos; to have courage.
G1761: Inward thought, reflection, plur: thoughts. From enthumeomai; deliberation.
G2123: Easier. Comparative of a compound of eu and kopos; better for toil, i.e. More facile.
G3855: To pass by, depart, pass away. From para and ago; to lead near, i.e. to go along or away.
G5058: A tax-collector's office, toll-house. Neuter of a presumed derivative of telones; a tax-gatherer's place of business.
G450: To raise up, set up; I rise from among (the) dead; I arise, appear. From ana and histemi; to stand up.
G345: To recline, especially at a dinner-table. From ana and keimai; to recline.
G4873: To recline at table with. From sun and anakeimai; to recline in company with.
G2068: Strengthened for a primary edo; used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by phago; to eat.
G3129: Prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, matheo, is used as an alternate in certain tenses; to learn.
G522: To take away, remove; pass: To be taken away, withdrawn. From apo and airo; to lift off, i.e. Remove.
G5501: Worse, more severe. Irregular comparative of kakos; from an obsolete equivalent cheres; more evil or aggravated.
G4978: A rent, as in a garment; a division, dissention. From schizo; a split or gap, literally or figuratively.
G4933: From sun and tereo; to keep closely together, i.e. to conserve; mentally, to remember.
G131: To suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood. From haima and rheo; to flow blood, i.e. Have a hoemorrhage.
G1427: Twelve; the usual way in which the Twelve apostles of Jesus are referred to. From duo and deka; two and ten, i.e. A dozen.
G2899: The fringe, edge, corner, tassel. Of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e., a fringe or tassel.
G2350: From thorubos; to be in tumult, i.e. Disturb, clamor.
G2877: A little girl, a young girl; a girl, maiden. Neuter of a presumed derivative of kore; a girl.
G1690: From en and brimaomai; to have indignation on, i.e. to blame, to sigh with chagrin, to sternly enjoin.
G1310: To report, publish abroad. From dia and a derivative of pheme; to report thoroughly, i.e. Divulgate.
G4697: To feel compassion, have pity on, be moved.
G4660: To flay, trouble, annoy, vex. Apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. to harass.
G4496: A primary verb; to fling (see in ekteino), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit; by extension, to disperse.
G4166: A shepherd; hence met: of the feeder, protector, and ruler of a flock of men. Of uncertain affinity; a shepherd.
G2040: A field-laborer; then: a laborer, workman in general. From ergon; a toiler; figuratively, a teacher.
G1189: To want for myself; I want, need; I beg, request, beseech, pray. Middle voice of deo; to beg, i.e. Petition.
G4341: To call to myself, summon. Middle voice from pros and kaleo; to call toward oneself, i.e. Summon, invite.
G652: From apostello; a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ.
G918: Of Chaldee origin; son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomoeus, a Christian apostle.
G2381: Thomas, also called Didymus, one of the Twelve. Of Chaldee origin; the twin; Thomas, a Christian.
G256: Alphaeus; apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi, and (b) father of James. Of Hebrew origin; Alphoeus, an Israelite.
G2280: Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles. Of uncertain origin; Thaddaeus, one of the Apostles.
G2581: A Canaanite. Of Chaldee origin; zealous; Cananites, an epithet.
G2469: Iscariot, surname of Judas. Of Hebrew origin; inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes, an epithet of Judas the traitor.
G770: To be weak (physically: then morally), To be sick. From asthenes; to be feeble.
G2932: (a) I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy, (b) I possess, win mastery over. A primary verb; to get, i.e. Acquire.
G4082: A sack, wallet for carrying provisions. Of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food.
G1621: To shake off; mid: I shake off from myself. From ek and tinasso; to shake violently.
G414: Endurable, tolerable. Comparative of a derivative of anechomai; more endurable.
G1116: Gomorrah, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea. Of Hebrew origin; Gomorrha, a place near the Dead Sea.
G185: (lit: unmixed) simple, unsophisticated, sincere, blameless. Unmixed, i.e. innocent.
G3146: To flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame; met: I chastise. From mastix; to flog.
G1881: Intrans. tenses: I rise up against. Middle voice from epi and anistemi; to stand up on, i.e. to attack.
G2289: To put to death, subdue; pass: To be in danger of death, be dead to, be rid of, be parted from. From thanatos to kill.
G1941: (a) To call (name) by a supplementary (additional, alternative) name, (b) mid: To call upon, appeal to, address.
G954: Beelzebul, a name of Satan, the chief of evil spirits. Of Chaldee origin; dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan.
G3615: One of a family, whether child or servant. From oikia; familiar, i.e. relatives.
G4453: To sell, exchange, barter. Probably ultimately from pelomai; to barter, i.e. To sell.
G787: A small coin equal to the tenth part of a drachma. Of Latin origin; an assarius or as, a Roman coin.
G3162: A sword. Probably feminine of a presumed derivative of mache; a knife, i.e. Dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment.
G1369: To cut asunder; met: I set at variance, make to be hostile. From a derivative of dis; to make apart, i.e. Sunder.
G3565: From a primary but obsolete verb nupto; a young married woman, including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife.
G4222: To cause to drink, give to drink; irrigate, water. From a derivative of the alternate of pino; to furnish drink, irrigate.
G3398: Little, small. Including the comparative mikroteros apparently a primary word; small (figuratively) dignity).
G1299: To give orders to, prescribe, arrange. From dia and tasso; to arrange thoroughly, i.e. institute, prescribe, etc.
G4328: To expect, wait for, await, think, anticipate. From pros and dokeuo; to anticipate; by implication, to await.
G308: To look up, recover my sight. From ana and blepo; to look up; by implication, to recover sight.
G5560: Lame, deprived of a foot, limping. Apparently a primary word; |halt|, i.e. Limping.
G2097: From eu and aggelos; to announce good news especially the gospel.
G2563: A reed; a reed-pen, reed-staff, measuring rod. Or uncertain affinity; a reed; by implication, a pen.
G4531: From salos; to waver, i.e. Agitate, rock, topple or destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite.
G3120: (a) soft, (b) of persons: soft, delicate, effeminate. Of uncertain affinity; soft, i.e. Fine; figuratively, a catamite.
G5409: To carry, wear, bear constantly. From phoros; to have a burden, i.e. to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment.
G971: From bios; to force, i.e. to crowd oneself, or to be seized.
G973: A forceful, violent man; one who is eager in pursuit. From biazo; a forcer, i.e. energetic.
G4377: From pros and phoneo; to sound towards, i.e. Address, exclaim, summon.
G832: To play the flute, pipe. From aulos; to play the flute.
G2354: Intrans: I lament, wail; trans: I bewail. From threnos; to bewail.
G2875: A primary verb; to |chop|; specially, to beat the breast in grief.
G5314: A glutton. From phago; a glutton.
G3630: An excessive wine-drinker. From oinos and a derivative of the alternate of pino; a tippler.
G5384: Friendly; subst: a friend, an associate. Properly, dear, i.e. A friend; actively, fond, i.e. Friendly.
G5523: Chorazin, a town of Galilee. Of uncertain derivation; Chorazin, a place in Palestine.
G5312: (a) I raise on high, lift up, (b) I exalt, set on high. From hupsos; to elevate.
G4908: Intelligent, prudent, wise, understanding, discerning. From suniemi; mentally put together, i.e. Sagacious.
G3516: From an obsolete particle ne- and epos; not speaking, i.e. An infant; figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian.
G2107: From a presumed compound of eu and the base of dokeo; satisfaction, i.e. delight, or kindness, wish, purpose.
G5412: To load, burden; pass: To be laden. From phortos; to load up, i.e. to overburden with ceremony.
G373: From ana and pauo; to repose (be exempt), remain); by implication, to refresh.
G5011: Humble, lowly, in position or spirit (in a good sense). Of uncertain derivation; depressed, i.e. humiliated.
G372: Rest, cessation from labor, refreshment. From anapano; intermission; by implication, recreation.
G5413: A burden; the freight of a ship. Diminutive of phortos; an invoice, i.e. a task or service.
G1645: Light, not burdensome. Probably akin to elauno and the base of elasson; light, i.e. Easy.
G5089: To pluck, pluck off. Perhaps akin to the alternate of haireomai, and thus to suro; to pull off.
G4286: From protithemai; a setting forth, i.e. proposal; specially, the show-bread as exposed before God.
G2613: To condemn, pass sentence upon. From kata and a derivative of dike; to adjudge against, i.e. Pronounce guilty.
G3584: Dry, withered; noun: dry land. From the base of xestes; arid; by implication, shrunken, earth.
G2723: To accuse, charge, prosecute. From kategoros; to be a plaintiff, i.e. To charge with some offence.
G1905: To interrogate, question, demand of. From epi and erotao; to ask for, i.e. Inquire, seek.
G1706: To fall in, be cast in, be involved in. From en and pipto; to fall on, i.e. to be entrapped by, or be overwhelmed with.
G4824: Neuter of a presumed derivative of sumboulos; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. The provincial assessors or lay-court.
G5318: Apparent, clear, visible, manifest; adv: clearly. From phaino; shining, i.e. Apparent; neuter publicly, externally.
G140: To choose. From a derivative of haireomai; to make a choice.
G2051: To contend, dispute, wrangle, strive. From eris; to wrangle.
G2905: To cry aloud, shout, exclaim. From krauge; to clamor.
G4937: From sun and the base of tribos; to crush completely, i.e. To shatter.
G2608: To break down (in pieces), crush, break into. From kata and the base of rhegnumi; to rend in pieces, i.e. Crack apart.
G5188: To raise smoke, smolder. Apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. Slowly consume without flame.
G4570: (a) I extinguish, quench, (b) I suppress, thwart. A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish.
G1679: To hope, hope for, expect, trust. From elpis; to expect or confide.
G1839: From ek and histemi; to put out of wits, i.e. Astound, or become astounded, insane.
G3307: From meros; to part, i.e. to apportion, bestow, share, or to disunite, differ.
G2049: (a) I make desolate, bring to desolation, destroy, waste, (b) of a person: I strip, rob. From eremos; to lay waste.
G5348: Apparently a primary verb; to be beforehand, i.e. Anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at.
G4632: A vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband).
G1210: To bind, tie, fasten; I impel, compel; I declare to be prohibited and unlawful. A primary verb; to bind.
G4650: Apparently from the same as skorpios; to dissipate, i.e. put to flight, waste, be liberal.
G165: From the same as aei; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity; by implication, the world; specially a Messianic period.
G2495: (Hebrew), Jonah, the Hebrew prophet. Of Hebrew origin; Jonas, the name of two Israelites.
G2785: A sea monster, huge sea fish, whale. Probably from the base of chasma; a huge fish.
G3536: A Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh, a city on the Tigris in Assyria. From Nineui; a Ninevite, i.e. Inhabitant of Nineveh.
G2632: To condemn, judge worthy of punishment. From kata and krino; to judge against, i.e. Sentence.
G3558: The south wind, the South. Of uncertain affinity; the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself.
G4009: (a) a boundary, limit, extremity, (b) an end, conclusion. From the same as peran; an extremity.
G4980: From schole; to take a holiday, i.e. Be at leisure for; figuratively, to be vacant.
G4563: To sweep, cleanse by sweeping. From a derivative of sairo; meaning a broom; to sweep.
G2885: To put into order; I decorate, deck, adorn. From kosmos; to put in proper order, i.e. Decorate; specially, to snuff.
G79: A sister, a woman (fellow-)member of a church, a Christian woman. Fem of adephos; a sister.
G123: Sea-coast, (sandy) beach; shore (of sea or lake), land. From aisso and hals (on which the waves dash).
G2719: To eat up, eat till it is finished, devour, squander, annoy, injure. From kata and esthio; to eat down, i.e. Devour.
G1816: To rise (spring) up out (of the ground). From ek and anatello; to start up out of the ground, i.e. Germinate.
G3583: To dry up, parch, be ripened, wither, waste away. From xeros; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature.
G4155: To choke, throttle, strangle; hence: I drown. Strengthened from pneo; to wheeze, i.e. to throttle or strangle.
G4394: Prophecy, prophesying; the gift of communicating and enforcing revealed truth. From prophetes; prediction.
G378: From ana and pleroo; to complete; by implication, to occupy, supply; figuratively, to accomplish.
G3975: To fatten, thicken; pass. fig: I become stupid, dull, unfeeling. From a derivative of pegnumi; to thicken, i.e. to fatten.
G2576: To close, shut the eyes. From a compound of kata and the base of musterion; to shut down, i.e. Close the eyes.
G4340: For a season, temporary. From pros and kairos; for the occasion only, i.e. Temporary.
G4149: From the base of pletho; wealth, i.e. money, possessions, or abundance, richness, valuable bestowment.
G4846: To choke utterly, as weeds do plants; I crowd upon. From sun and pnigo; to strangle completely, i.e. to drown, or to crowd.
G3908: From para and tithemi; to place alongside, i.e. Present; by implication, to deposit.
G985: Intrans: I sprout; trans: I cause to sprout, make to grow up. From blastos; to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit.
G1610: To root out, pluck up by the roots. From ek and rhizoo; to uproot.
G4885: To grow together. From sun and auzano; to increase together.
G2798: A young tender shoot, then: a branch; met: of descendants. From klao; a twig or bough.
G1470: To hide in, mix with. From en and krupto; to conceal in, i.e. Incorporate with.
G4568: A large measure equal to nearly three English gallons. Of Hebrew origin; a certain measure for things dry.
G2220: To leaven, ferment. From zume; to cause to ferment.
G2044: (lit: I belch forth, hence) I utter, declare. Of uncertain affinity; to belch, i.e. to speak out.
G1285: To make clear, explain fully. From dia and saphes; to clear thoroughly, i.e. declare.
G4930: A completion, consummation, end. From sunteleo; entire completion, i.e. Consummation.
G4625: A snare, stumbling-block, cause for error. Scandal; probably from a derivative of kampto; a trap-stick, i.e. Snare.
G1584: To shine forth (out). From ek and lampo; to be resplendent.
G1713: A merchant, trader; one on a journey. From en and the base of poreuomai; a tradesman.
G4186: Of great value, very costly, very precious. From polus and time; extremely valuable.
G4097: A reduplicated and prolonged form of prao; contracted from perao; to traffic, i.e. Dispose of as merchandise or into slavery.
G4522: A fishing-net. From a derivative of satto meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle; a |seine| for fishing.
G307: To draw up, as a net to shore. From ana and a derivative of the base of basis; to cause to go up, i.e. Haul.
G873: To rail off, separate, place apart. From apo and horizo; to set off by boundary, i.e. limit, exclude, appoint, etc.
G3100: From mathetes; intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. Enrol as scholar.
G3332: To change my position, depart, remove. From meta and airo; to betake oneself, i.e. Remove.
G3968: Fatherland, one's native place. From parasemos; a father-land, i.e. Native town; heavenly home.
G5045: A carpenter, an artisan. From the base of timoria; an artificer, i.e., a craftsman in wood.
G820: Without honor, despised. (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured.
G570: Unbelief, unfaithfulness, distrust. From apistos; faithlessness, i.e. disbelief, or unfaithfulness.
G5076: A tetrarch, ruler over a fourth part of a region. From tessares and archo; the ruler of a fourth part of a country.
G659: To lay off or aside, renounce, stow away, put. From apo and tithemi; to put away.
G1077: A birthday celebration. Neuter plural of a derivative of genesis; birthday ceremonies.
G700: To please, with the idea of willing service rendered to others; hence almost: I serve. Probably from airo; to be agreeable.
G4264: From pro and a reduplicated form of biazo; to force forward, i.e. Bring to the front, instigate.
G3076: To pain, grieve, vex. From lupe; to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad.
G4430: A fall; a carcass, corpse, dead body. From the alternate of pipto; a ruin, i.e., lifeless body.
G3979: On foot, by land. Dative case feminine of a derivative of pous; foot-wise, i.e. By walking.
G1033: Food of any kind. From the base of bibrosko; food, especially articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law.
G4134: Full, abounding in, complete, completely occupied with. From pletho; replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete.
G4000: Five thousand. From pentakis and chilioi; five times a thousand.
G4712: Or masculine stadios from the base of histemi; a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course.
G1727: Opposite, opposed, contrary; the adversary. From enanti; opposite; figuratively, antagonistic.
G5401: (a) fear, terror, alarm, (b) the object or cause of fear, (c) reverence, respect. From a primary phebomai; alarm or fright.
G2670: From kata and a derivative of the same as Pontos; to plunge down, i.e. Submerge.
G1949: To lay hold of, take hold of, seize (sometimes with beneficent, sometimes with hostile, intent).
G1365: To waver, doubt, hesitate. From dis; properly, to duplicate, i.e. to waver.
G2869: To abate, cease raging, be stilled. From kopos; to tire, i.e. to relax.
G1295: From dia and sozo; to save thoroughly, i.e. to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.
G3845: To transgress, violate, depart, desert. From para and the base of basis; to go contrary to, i.e. Violate a command.
G3862: An instruction, tradition. From paradidomi; transmission, i.e. a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law.
G4245: Comparative of presbus; older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist or Christian |presbyter|.
G2551: To speak evil of, curse, revile, abuse. From a compound of kakos and logos; to revile.
G5623: To help, benefit, do good, be useful (to), profit. From the same as opheleia; to be useful, i.e. To benefit.
G208: To annul, make of no effect, cancel. To invalidate.
G4576: To reverence, worship, adore. Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. Adore.
G1778: An injunction, ordinance, precept. From entellomai; an injunction, i.e. Religious precept.
G2840: To make unclean, pollute, desecrate, mid: I regard (treat) as unclean. From koinos; to make profane.
G5451: A plant, that which is planted. From phuteuo; trans-planting, i.e. a shrub or vegetable.
G5452: To plant, set. From a derivative of phuo; to set out in the earth, i.e. Implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine.
G3595: A leader, guide; met: an instructor, teacher. From hodos and hegeomai; a conductor (teacher).
G188: Even now. Accusative case of a noun akin to ake and meaning the same; adverbially, just now, i.e. Still.
G5419: To declare, explain, interpret. Probably akin to phrasso through the idea of defining; to indicate, i.e., to expound.
G801: Unintelligent, without wisdom, unwise, undiscerning (implying probably moral defect). By implication, wicked.
G1531: To journey in(to), I go in(to), enter, intervene. From eis and poreuomai; to enter.
G856: A drain, latrine. From a compound of apo and the base of hedraios; a place of sitting apart, i.e. A privy.
G5577: False testimony, false witness. From pseudomartur; untrue testimony.
G5478: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician. From Chanaan; a Chanaanoean, or native of gentile Palestine.
G5132: Probably contracted from tessares and peze; a table or stool, usually for food; also a counter for money.
G2948: Crippled, lame, especially in the hands. From the same as kulioo; rocking about, i.e. Crippled.
G4357: From pros and meno; to stay further, i.e. Remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in.
G3523: Fasting, not eating. From the inseparable negative particle ne- and esthio; not eating, i.e. Abstinent from food.
G1590: To loose, release, unloose (as a bow-string), relax, enfeeble; pass: To be faint, grow weary. From ek and luo; to relax.
G2168: From eucharistos; to be grateful, i.e. to express gratitude; specially, to say grace at a meal.
G5070: Four thousand. From the multiplicative adverb of tessares and chilioi; four times a thousand.
G3093: Magdala, Magadan, a proper name. Of Chaldee origin; the tower; Magdala, a place in Palestine.
G1925: To show, display, point out, indicate; I prove, demonstrate. From epi and deiknuo; to exhibit.
G2105: Fair weather, good weather. Feminine from eu and the alternate of Zeus; a clear sky, i.e. Fine weather.
G4768: To be gloomy, have a somber countenance, be shocked. From the same as stugnetos; to render gloomy, i.e. glower.
G1252: From dia and krino; to separate thoroughly, i.e. to withdraw from, or oppose; figuratively, to discriminate, or hesitate.
G1950: To forget, neglect. Middle voice from epi and lanthano; to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect.
G1260: To reason (with), debate (with), consider. From dia and logizomai; to reckon thoroughly, i.e. to deliberate.
G920: Bar-Jonas, son of Jonas, the surname of Simon Peter. Of Chaldee origin; son of Jonas; Bar-jonas, an Israelite.
G1577: From a compound of ek and a derivative of kaleo; a calling out, i.e. a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation.
G2729: To prevail against, overpower, get the upper hand. From kata and ischuo; to overpower.
G1291: To give a commission (instructions), order; To admonish, prohibit.
G1163: Third person singular active present of deo; also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is Necessary.
G4355: (a) I take to myself, (b) I take aside, (c) I welcome. From pros and lambano; to take to oneself, i.e. Use, lead, admit.
G2436: Perhaps from the alternate form of haireomai; cheerful, i.e. Propitious; adverbially God be gracious!, i.e. far be it.
G5426: (a) I think, (b) I think, judge, (c) I direct the mind to, seek for, (d) I observe, (e) I care for.
G533: From apo and arneomai; to deny utterly, i.e. Disown, abstain.
G465: An exchange, purchasing price. From a compound of anti and allasso; an equivalent or ransom.
G3339: To transform, transfigure. From meta and morphoo; to transform.
G4814: To talk with, discuss. From sun and laleo; to talk together, i.e. Converse.
G4633: A tent, booth, tabernacle, abode, dwelling, mansion, habitation. Apparently akin to skeuos and skia; a tent or cloth hut.
G1982: To overshadow, envelop; to cast a shade upon, i.e. to envelop in a haze of brilliancy.
G1120: From a compound of gonu and the alternate of pipto; to fall on the knee.
G1294: To pervert, corrupt, oppose, distort. From dia and strepho; to distort, i.e. misinterpret, or corrupt.
G430: To endure, bear with, have patience with, suffer, admit, persist.
G101: To be impossible; I am unable. From adunatos; to be unable, i.e. impossible.
G4962: To roll or gather together. From sun and strepho; to twist together, i.e. Collect.
G1323: A double-drachma, two drachmae, a Greek silver coin. From dis and drachme; a double drachma.
G4399: To anticipate, forestall. From pro and phthano; to get an earlier start of, i.e. Anticipate.
G245: From allos; another's, i.e. Not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile.
G1658: Free, delivered from obligation. Probably from the alternate of erchomai; unrestrained, i.e. not a slave, or exempt.
G44: A fish-hook. From the same as agkale; a hook.
G4715: From the base of kauchesis; a stander, i.e., a stater or certain coin.
G5013: To make or bring low, humble, humiliate; pass: To be humbled. From tapeinos; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate.
G3458: A millstone, mill. Probably ultimately from the base of molis; a |mill|, i.e., a grinder.
G2910: To hang, hang up, suspend; mid: To be hanging, hang. A prolonged form of a primary verb; to hang.
G3442: One-eyed, with one eye only. From monos and ophthalmos; one-eyed.
G264: Perhaps from a and the base of meros; properly, to miss the mark, i.e. to err, especially to sin.
G1651: (a) I reprove, rebuke, discipline, (b) I expose, show to be guilty. Of uncertain affinity; to confute, admonish.
G3878: From para and akouo; to mishear, i.e. to disobey.
G4856: To agree with, harmonize with, agree together. From sumphonos; to be harmonious, i.e. to accord or stipulate.
G4229: A thing done, a deed, action; a matter, an affair. From prasso; a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object.
G4868: To compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning. From sun and airo; to make up together, i.e. to compute.
G3463: Plural of an apparently primary word; ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many.
G5007: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of tlao; a balance, i.e. a certain weight or |talent|.
G3114: From the same as makrothumos; to be long-spirited, i.e. forbearing or patient.
G4889: From sun and doulos; a co-slave, i.e. Servitor or ministrant of the same master.
G3784: Or, its prolonged form opheileo probably from the base of ophelos; to owe; figuratively, to be under obligation; morally, to fail in duty.
G3782: A debt, a duty, what is due. From opheilo; indebtedness, i.e. a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. duty.
G930: One who tortures, a tormentor, jailor. From basanizo; a torturer.
G2936: To create, form, shape, make, always of God. Probably akin to ktaomai; to fabricate, i.e. Found.
G4801: To yoke together, unite (as man and wife). From sun and the base of zeugos; to yoke together, i.e. conjoin.
G4641: Feminine of a compound of skleros and kardia; hard-heartedness, i.e., destitution of perception.
G2135: From eune and echo; a castrated person; by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain.
G2134: To make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate. From eunouchos; to castrate.
G5576: To testify falsely, bear false witness. From pseudomartur; to be an untrue testifier, i.e. Offer falsehood in evidence.
G5442: Probably from phule through the idea of isolation; to watch, i.e. Be on guard; by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid.
G5302: From husteros; to be later, i.e. to be inferior; generally, to fall short.
G5225: To begin, am, exist, be in possession. From hupo and archomai; to begin under, i.e. Come into existence; expletively, to exist (verb).
G4145: Rich, abounding in, wealthy; subst: a rich man. From ploutos; wealthy; figuratively, abounding with.
G5169: A hole; the eye of a needle. From a derivative of the base of trumalia; an aperture, i.e. A needle's eye.
G102: Of persons: incapable; of things: impossible; either the inability, or that which is impossible. Passively, impossible.
G3824: A new birth, regeneration, renewal. From palin and genesis; rebirth, i.e. spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration.
G1542: A hundredfold. From hekaton and a presumed derivative of plasso; a hundred times.
G3409: To hire out, mid: I hire, engage. From misthos; to let out for wages, i.e. to hire.
G1111: To whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smoldering discontent). Of uncertain derivation; to grumble.
G2083: A companion, comrade, friend. From etes; a comrade.
G922: Probably from the same as basis; weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority.
G2176: From eu and onoma; properly, well-named, i.e. The left; neuter as adverbial, at the left hand.
G23: To be angry, incensed. From agan and achthos; to be greatly afflicted, i.e. indignant.
G2634: To exercise authority over, overpower, master. From kata and kurieuo; to lord against, i.e. Control, subjugate.
G2715: To have (exercise) power (authority) over. From kata and exousiazo; to have full privilege over.
G1249: Probably from an obsolete diako; an attendant, i.e. a waiter; specially, a Christian teacher and pastor.
G2410: Jericho, a city a little north of the Dead Sea. Of Hebrew origin; Jericho, a place in Palestine.
G4623: To keep silence, be silent, either voluntarily or involuntarily. From siope; to be dumb; figuratively, to be calm.
G3659: An eye. From optanomai; a sight, i.e. the eye.
G5455: From phone; to emit a sound; by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation.
G1636: An olive tree; the Mount of Olives. Feminine of a presumed derivative from an obsolete primary; an olive.
G4454: A colt, young ass, foal. Apparently a primary word; a |foal| or |filly|, i.e., a young ass.
G4622: Zion, the hill; used for Jerusalem or heaven. Of Hebrew origin; Sion, a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church.
G1910: From epi and the base of basis; to walk upon, i.e. Mount, ascend, embark, arrive.
G5268: A beast of burden, an ass or mule. Neuter of a compound of hupo and zugos; an animal under the yoke, i.e., a donkey.
G4929: To arrange with, direct, appoint, prescribe, ordain. From sun and tasso; to arrange jointly, i.e. to direct.
G1940: To sit upon, cause to sit upon. From epi and kathizo; to seat upon.
G4766: To spread, make a bed. Or simpler stronnuo, prolongation from a still simpler stroo, ; to |strew, | i.e. Spread.
G5310: Highest, most high, the heights. Superlative from the base of hupsos; highest, i.e. the Supreme, or the heavens.
G4579: To shake; fig: I agitate, stir up. Apparently a primary verb; to rock, i.e. to agitate; figuratively, to throw into a tremor.
G2690: To overturn, overthrow. From kata and strepho; to turn upside down, i.e. Upset.
G4693: A cave, den, hideout. Neuter of a presumed derivative of speos; a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort.
G2297: Wonderful, admirable; subst: a wonder. From thauma; wondrous, i.e. a miracle.
G2337: (a) I give suck, (b) I suck. From thele; to suckle, to suck.
G136: Praise. Apparently a prime word; properly, a story, but used in the sense of epainos; praise.
G835: To lodge in the open, lodge, pass the night. Middle voice from aule; to pass the night.
G3338: From meta and the middle voice of melo; to care afterwards, i.e. Regret.
G4204: A prostitute; met: an idolatrous community. Feminine of pornos; a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater.
G4060: To place or put around, clothe; fig: I bestow, confer. From peri and tithemi; to place around; by implication, to present.
G3736: To dig, dig out, excavate. Apparently a primary verb; to |burrow| in the ground, i.e. Dig.
G1554: To give out, let; middle: I let out for my own advantage. From ek and didomi; to give forth, i.e. to lease.
G589: To be away from home, go into another country, be away, be abroad. From apodemos; to go abroad, i.e. Visit a foreign land.
G1194: To flay, flog, scourge, beat. A primary verb; properly, to flay, i.e. to scourge, or to thrash.
G3036: To stone, cast stones (at), kill by stoning. From a compound of lithos and ballo; to throw stones, i.e. Lapidate.
G1788: From en and the base of trope; to invert, i.e. in a good sense, to respect; or in a bad one, to confound.
G2818: From kleros and the base of nomos (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. Inheritor; by implication, a possessor.
G1124: (a) a writing, (b) a passage of scripture; plur: the scriptures. A document, i.e. Holy Writ.
G593: To reject after testing (examination), disqualify. From apo and dokimazo; to disapprove, i.e. to repudiate.
G2298: To be wondered at, wonderful, marvelous. From thaumazo; wondered at, i.e. wonderful.
G4917: To break, break in pieces, crush, shatter. From sun and thlao; to dash together, i.e. Shatter.
G3039: To crush to powder, scatter like chaff. From likmos, the equivalent of liknon; to winnow, i.e., to triturate.
G1062: A marriage, wedding, wedding-ceremony; plur: a wedding-feast. Of uncertain affinity; nuptials.
G712: Breakfast or a mid-day meal. Apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as arrhen; the best meal (|early|), i.e. Luncheon.
G4619: Fattened; subst: a fatling, cattle. From a derivative of sitos; grained, i.e. Fatted.
G2380: A primary verb; properly, to rush, i.e. to sacrifice; by extension to immolate.
G272: To neglect, be careless of, disregard. To be careless of.
G1711: Trading, trade, trafficking, business. Feminine from emporos; traffic.
G4753: An army, detachment of troops. From strateuomai; an armament, i.e. a body of troops.
G1714: To burn, set on fire, suffer inflammation. From en and pretho; to enkindle, i.e. Set on fire.
G1327: A meeting-place of roads, a public spot in a city. From dia and exodos; an outlet through, i.e. Probably an open square.
G4130: To fill, fulfill, complete. A prolonged form of a primary pleo to |fill| (imbue, influence, supply); specially, to fulfil.
G3802: To ensnare, entrap, entangle. From pagis; to ensnare.
G2265: The Herodians, the partisans of Herod (Antipas). Plural of a derivative of Herodes; Herodians, i.e. Partisans of Herod.
G3546: Money, coin. From nomizo; what is reckoned as of value, i.e. Current coin.
G1504: An image, likeness, bust. From eiko; a likeness, i.e. statue, profile, or representation, resemblance.
G1923: An inscription, title, label. From epigrapho; an inscription.
G386: A rising again, resurrection. From anistemi; a standing up again, i.e. a resurrection from death (its author), or a recovery.
G1918: From epi and a derivative of gamos; to form affinity with, i.e. in a levirate way.
G1061: To give in marriage. From gamos; to espouse.
G1271: From dia and nous; deep thought, properly, the faculty, by implication, its exercise.
G5606: The shoulder. Perhaps from the alternate of phero; the shoulder.
G5111: To dare, endure, be bold, have courage, make up the mind. From tolma; to venture; by implication, to be courageous.
G1195: To bind, put in chains, tie together. From a derivative of desmeo; to be a binder, i.e. To enchain, to tie on.
G926: Heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met; violent, oppressive. From the same as baros; weighty, i.e. burdensome, grave.
G1419: Difficult to carry, oppressive. From dus- and a derivative of bastazo; oppressive.
G2795: To set in motion, move, remove, excite, stir up. From kio; to stir, literally or figuratively.
G4115: To enlarge, make broad; met: of the growth of tenderness and love. From platus; to widen.
G5440: Neuter of a derivative of phulasso; a guard-case, i.e. |phylactery| for wearing slips of Scripture texts.
G3170: (a) I enlarge, lengthen, (b) I increase, magnify, extol. From megas; to make great, i.e. Increase or extol.
G4411: From protos and klisia; a reclining first at the dinner-bed, i.e. Preeminence at meals.
G1173: A dinner, an afternoon or evening meal. From the same as dapane; dinner, i.e. The chief meal.
G4410: A chief (most honorable) seat. From protos and kathedra; a sitting first, i.e. Preeminence in council.
G2519: A leader, teacher, guide, master. From a compound of kata and hegeomai; a guide, i.e. a teacher.
G4339: From the alternate of proserchomai; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e., an acceder to Judaism.
G1362: Double, two-fold. From dis and the base of pleion; two-fold.
G3485: A temple, a shrine, that part of the temple where God himself resides. From a primary naio; a fane, shrine, temple.
G586: To take off (deduct) a tenth part (of my property) (and give it away), pay tithe. From apo and dekatoo; to tithe.
G2238: Mint, peppermint. Neuter of the compound of the same as hedeos and osme; a sweet-scented plant, i.e. Mint.
G432: Anise, dill. Probably of foreign origin; dill.
G2951: Cumin, a plant used as a spice. Of foreign origin; dill or fennel.
G1368: To strain, put through a sieve. From dia and hulizo hoo-lid'-zo; to strain out.
G2971: Apparently a derivative of the base of kentron and a derivative of optanomai; a mosquito.
G2666: To drink down, swallow, devour, destroy, consume. From kata and pino; to drink down, i.e. Gulp entire.
G1855: (a) from outside, from without, (b) outside, both as adj. and prep; with article: the outside. From exo; external(-ly).
G3953: Prop: a dainty side-dish; meton: a plate, dish, platter. From para and the base of opsarion; a side-dish.
G5611: Fair, beautiful, blooming. From hora; belonging to the right hour or season, i.e. flourishing (figuratively).
G167: Uncleanness, impurity. From akathartos; impurity, physically or morally.
G6: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain. Of Hebrew origin; Abel, the son of Adam.
G914: Of Hebrew origin; Barachias, an Israelite.
G1996: To collect, gather together, assemble. From epi and sunago; to collect upon the same place.
G5158: From the same as trope; a turn, i.e. mode or style; figuratively, deportment or character.
G3733: A bird, fowl, hen. Probably from a prolonged form of the base of oros; a bird, i.e., a hen.
G3619: Feminine of a compound of oikos and the base of doma; architecture, i.e. a structure; figuratively, confirmation.
G3952: From the present participle of pareimi; a being near, i.e. Advent; physically, aspect.
G2360: To disturb, agitate; pass: To be troubled, alarmed. From threomai to wail; to clamor, i.e. to frighten.
G5604: The pain of childbirth, acute pain, severe agony, a snare. Akin to odune; a pang or throe, especially of childbirth.
G4129: To increase, multiply. From another form of plethos; to increase.
G5594: To cool, pass: I grow cold. A primary verb; to breathe, i.e. to chill.
G3625: Feminine participle present passive of oikeo; land, i.e. The globe; specially, the Roman empire.
G1158: Daniel. Of Hebrew origin; Daniel, an Israelite.
G946: An abominable thing, an accursed thing. From bdelusso; a detestation, i.e. idolatry.
G5437: Flight, fleeing. From pheugo; a fleeing, i.e. Escape.
G2856: (lit: I maim, mutilate), I cut short, shorten, abbreviate. From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to dock, i.e. abridge.
G5580: A false Christ, pretended Messiah. From pseudes and Christos; a spurious Messiah.
G4302: To tell (say) beforehand, forewarn, declare, tell plainly. From pro and lego; to say beforehand, i.e. Predict, forewarn.
G796: A flash of lightning, brightness, luster. From astrapto; lightning; by analogy, glare.
G206: The end, extremity. Neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of akmen; the extremity.
G229: To grind. From the same as aleuron; to grind.
G1127: (a) I am awake (in the night), watch, (b) I am watchful, on the alert, vigilant. From egeiro; to keep awake, i.e. Watch.
G1439: To allow, permit, let alone, leave. Of uncertain affinity; to let be, i.e. Permit or leave alone.
G4103: Trustworthy, faithful, believing. From peitho; objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful.
G2525: From kata and histemi; to place down, i.e. to designate, constitute, convoy.
G3184: To be intoxicated with wine, be drunk. From another form of methe; to drink to intoxication, i.e. Get drunk.
G1371: From a compound of a derivative of dis and a derivative of temno; to bisect, i.e. to flog severely.
G3573: To nod in sleep, be drowsy, slumber. From a presumed derivative of neuo; to nod, i.e. to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay.
G3379: Or me pote from me and pote; not ever; also if ever.
G714: To keep off, assist; I suffice; pass: To be satisfied. Apparently a primary verb; properly, to ward off, i.e. to avail.
G694: Neuter of a presumed derivative of arguros; silvery, i.e. cash; specially, a silverling.
G3636: Slothful, backward, hesitating; of things: irksome. From okneo; tardy, i.e. Indolent; irksome.
G1131: Rarely: stark-naked; generally: wearing only the under-garment; bare, open, manifest; mere. Of uncertain affinity; nude.
G2672: To curse. Middle voice from katara; to execrate; by analogy, to doom.
G772: (lit: not strong), (a) weak (physically, or morally), (b) infirm, sick. Strengthless.
G2851: Chastisement, punishment, torment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation. From kolazo; penal infliction.
G2351: (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, outcry, (b) riot, disturbance. From the base of throeo; a disturbance.
G211: Neuter of alabastros, the name of a stone; properly, an |alabaster| box, i.e. a perfume vase.
G2708: To pour (down) upon. From kata and cheo; to pour down.
G3930: From para and echo; to hold near, i.e. Present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion.
G2873: From kopto; a cut, i.e. toil, literally or figuratively; by implication, pains.
G1779: To embalm, prepare for burial. From a compound of en and taphos; to inswathe with cerements for interment.
G3422: Reminder, memorial; a remembrance offering. From mnemoneuo; a reminder, i.e. Record.
G1170: So and so, such a one, where the name of the person is known but not used. Probably from the same as deinos; so and so.
G1686: To dip into. From en and bapto; to whelm on, i.e. Wet By contact with a fluid.
G5165: A deep dish, platter, bowl. Neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl.
G859: A sending away, a letting go, a release, pardon, complete forgiveness. From aphiemi; freedom; pardon.
G5214: To sing, sing hymns to, praise. From humnos; to hymn, i.e. Sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate in song.
G3960: To smite, strike (as with a sword), smite to death, afflict. Probably prolongation from paio; to knock.
G5564: A place, piece of land, field, property, estate. Diminutive of chora; a spot or plot of ground.
G85: To feel fear, lack courage, be distressed, troubled. From a derivative of adeo; to be in distress.
G4036: Very sorrowful, greatly grieved. From peri and lupe; grieved all around, i.e. Intensely sad.
G4281: To go forward, go on, advance; I go before, precede. From pro and erchomai; to go onward, precede.
G4289: Eager, ready, willing, prompt. From pro and thumos; forward in spirit, i.e. Predisposed; neuter alacrity.
G916: To weight, load, burden, lit. and met. From barus; to weigh down.
G3063: Finally, from now on, henceforth, beyond that. Neuter singular of the same as loipoy; something remaining.
G3586: From another form of the base of xestes; timber; by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance.
G2705: To kiss affectionately. From kata and phileo; to kiss earnestly.
G3918: From para and eimi; to be near, i.e. At hand; neuter present participle time being, or property.
G645: From apo and spao; to drag forth, i.e. unsheathe, or relatively retire.
G4815: From sun and lambano; to clasp, i.e. Seize; specially, to conceive; by implication, to aid.
G2516: To be sitting, sit down, be seated. From kata and the base of hedraios; to sit down.
G5575: A false witness. From pseudes and a kindred form of martus; a spurious witness, i.e. Bearer of untrue testimony.
G2649: To give evidence (bear witness) against. From kata and martureo; to testify against.
G1844: To adjure, put to oath; I exorcise. From ek and horkizo; to exact an oath, i.e. Conjure.
G1284: To tear asunder, burst, rend. From dia and rhegnumi; to tear asunder.
G2852: To strike with the fist, buffet; hence: I mistreat violently. From a derivative of the base of kolazo; to rap with the fist.
G3817: To strike, smite, sting. A primary verb; to hit; specially, to sting.
G3814: A female slave, maidservant, maid, young girl. Feminine diminutive of pais; a girl, i.e., a female slave or servant.
G1057: A Galilean, an inhabitant of Galilee. From Galilaia; Galilean or belonging to Galilea.
G4440: From pule; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule.
G2981: (in classical Greek: babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech, dialect. From laleo; talk.
G2653: To curse, devote to destruction. From kata and anathematizo; to imprecate.
G5092: A price, honor. From tino; a value, i.e. Money paid, or valuables; by analogy, esteem, or the dignity itself.
G2763: A potter. From keramos; a potter.
G5027: A burial, burial place. Feminine from thapto; burial.
G2505: Just as. From kata and the neuter plural of hos; according to which things, i.e. Just as.
G1486: To be accustomed, custom, what was customary. A primary verb; to be used; neuter perfect participle usage.
G1978: Notable, conspicuous. From epi and some form of the base of semaino; remarkable, i.e. eminent.
G968: From the base of basis; a step, i.e. Foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. A tribunal.
G3982: A primary verb; to convince; by analogy, to pacify or conciliate; reflexively or passively, to assent, to rely.
G633: To wash dirt off. From apo and nipto; to wash off.
G5417: To flagellate, scourge. From a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. Lash as a public punishment.
G1562: From ek and the base of duno; to cause to sink out of, i.e. to divest.
G2847: Crimson, scarlet, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak. From kokkos; crimson-colored.
G5511: A short cloak, worn by military officers and soldiers. Of uncertain derivation; a military cloak.
G4120: To weave together, plait, twist, braid. A primary word; to twine or braid.
G4735: A crown, garland, honor, glory. From an apparently primary stepho; a chaplet, literally or figuratively.
G2956: Belonging to Cyrene, a Cyrenaean. From Kurene; i.e. Cyrenaean, i.e. Inhabitant of Cyrene.
G1115: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem. Of Chaldee origin; the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem.
G3396: To mix, mingle. A primary verb; to mix.
G5521: Gall, bitter herbs. Feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as Chloe; |gall| or bile, i.e. poison or an anodyne.
G1266: To divide up into parts, break up; I distribute. From dia and merizo; to partition thoroughly.
G2819: (a) a lot, (b) a portion assigned; hence: a portion of the people of God assigned to one's care, a congregation.
G3899: To go past, pass by, pass along by. From para and poreuomai; to travel near.
G4957: To crucify together with. From sun and stauroo; to impale in company with.
G310: To shout upwards, cry out, raise my voice. From ana and boao; to halloo.
G2241: Eli, my God (Hebrew). Of Hebrew origin; my God.
G2982: (Hebrew), why. Or lamma lam-mah'; of Hebrew origin; lama.
G4518: Thou hast forsaken me. Of Chaldee or; thou hast left me; sabachthani, a cry of distress.
G5143: Apparently a primary verb; which uses dremo drem'-o as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily.
G3690: Vinegar, sour wine mixed with water, a common drink of Roman soldiers. From oxus; vinegar, i.e. Sour wine.
G2665: From a compound of kata and a congener of petomai; something spread thoroughly, i.e. the door screen in the Jewish Temple.
G4977: To rend, divide asunder, cleave. Apparently a primary verb; to split or sever.
G1718: To make visible (manifest); hence: I report (inform) against; pass: I appear before. From emphanes; to exhibit or disclose.
G3094: Magdalene, a woman of Magdala. Feminine of a derivative of Magdala; a female Magdalene, i.e. Inhabitant of Magdala.
G707: Arimathea, a place in Palestine. Of Hebrew origin; Arimathaea, a place in Palestine.
G1794: To wrap up, roll round, envelop. From en and tulisso; to entwine, i.e. Wind up in.
G2998: To hew stones, cut stones. From the same as the first part of laxeutos and the base of tomoteros; to quarry.
G3904: The day of preparation, the day before the Sabbath, Friday. As if from paraskeuazo; readiness.
G4106: Feminine of planos; objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety.
G4972: To seal, set a seal upon. From sphragis; to stamp for security or preservation; by implication, to keep secret, to attest.
G2020: To dawn, be near commencing. A form of epiphauo; to begin to grow light.
G617: To roll away. From apo and kulioo; to roll away.
G2397: Form, outward appearance. From eido; a sight, i.e. Aspect.
G275: Free from anxiety (though anxiety is rather too strong a word) or care. Not anxious.
G5021: A prolonged form of a primary verb; to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. Assign or dispose.
G2415: An inhabitant of Jerusalem. From Hierosoluma; a Hierosolymite, i.e. Inhabitant of Hierosolyma.
G2955: To bend, stoop down, bow the head. Probably from the base of kuma; to bend forward.
G2342: Properly: a wild beast, hence: any animal; met: a brute. Diminutive from the same as thera; a dangerous animal.
G349: To shout aloud, cry out. From ana and krazo; to scream up.
G3479: Of Nazareth, a Nazarene. From Nazareth; a Nazarene, i.e. Inhabitant of Nazareth.
G4682: To convulse, throw into spasms. Prolongation from spairo; to mangle, i.e. Convluse with epilepsy.
G2284: I amaze; pass: I am amazed (almost terrified). From thambos; to stupefy, i.e. Astound.
G2004: To give order, command, charge. From epi and tasso; to arrange upon, i.e. Order.
G2621: From kata and keimai; to lie down, i.e. be sick; specially, to recline at a meal.
G1416: To sink, set (as the sun). Or dumi doo'-mee prolonged forms of an obsolete primary duo doo'-o to go down.
G2614: To hunt down, follow closely. From kata and dioko; to hunt down, i.e. Search for.
G237: From another place, by another way. From allos; from elsewhere.
G2969: From kome and polis; an unwalled city.
G648: To unroof, take the roof off. From apo and a derivative of stege; to unroof.
G1846: (a) I dig out, hence: I open up, (b) I gouge. From ek and orusso; to dig out, i.e. to extract, remove.
G5465: To let down, lower, slacken, loosen. From the base of chasma; to lower.
G1976: To sew (on). From epi and the base of rhaphis; to stitch upon, i.e. Fasten with the needle.
G8: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time. Of Hebrew origin; Abiathar, an Israelite.
G3906: To watch, observe scrupulously. From para and tereo; to inspect alongside, i.e. Note insidiously or scrupulously.
G2554: To do harm, do wrong, do evil, commit sin. From kakopoios; to be a bad-doer, i.e. to injure, or to sin.
G4818: To be moved to grief by sympathy. From sun and lupeo; to afflict jointly, i.e. sorrow at someone.
G4128: A multitude, crowd, great number, assemblage. From pletho; a fulness, i.e. A large number, throng, populace.
G2401: Idumea, Edom, a district of Arabia, immediately south of Judea. Of Hebrew origin; Idumaea, a region East of Palestine.
G4342: To persist, persevere in, continue steadfast in; I wait upon.
G1968: To fall upon, press upon, light upon, come over. From epi and pipto; to embrace or seize.
G3687: From onoma; to name, i.e. Assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess.
G993: Boanerges, sons of thunder. Of Chaldee origin; sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles.
G3537: A basin for washing hands or feet. From nipto; a ewer.
G4739: To stand fast, stand firm, persevere. From the perfect tense of histemi; to be stationary, i.e. to persevere.
G3858: To receive, accept, acknowledge. From para and dechomai; to accept near, i.e. Admit or delight in.
G614: Hidden away, secret, stored up. From apokrupto; secret; by implication, treasured.
G3373: To lengthen, extend, grow. From mekos; to lengthen, i.e. to enlarge.
G844: Of its own accord. From autos and the same as maten; self-moved, i.e. Spontaneous.
G1956: To loose, release; I solve, settle, explain, interpret, decide. From epi and luo; to solve further, i.e. to explain, decide.
G2978: A sudden storm, squall, whirlwind, hurricane. Of uncertain derivation; a whirlwind.
G4344: A pillow or cushion. Neuter of a presumed compound of pros and kephale; something for the head, i.e. A cushion.
G1326: To wake out of sleep, arouse in general, stir up. From dia and egeiro; to wake fully; i.e. Arouse.
G1086: From Gerasene. Of Hebrew origin; a Gergesene or one of the aborigines of Palestine.
G2731: A dwelling, abode, habitation. From katoikeo; residence.
G1288: To tear apart, burst. From dia and spao; to draw apart, i.e. Sever or dismember.
G1150: To tame, subdue, involving obedience and restraint. A variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; to tame.
G2629: To cut up, cut in pieces, mangle, wound. From kata and kopto; to chop down, i.e. Mangle.
G3726: To adjure by, charge solemnly by. From horkos; to put on oath, i.e. Make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin.
G1367: Two thousand. From dis and chilioi; two thousand.
G2439: To clothe, provide clothing for; pass: To be clothed. From himation; to dress.
G4993: To be of sound mind, be sober-minded, exercise self-control. From sophron; to be of sound mind, i.e. Sane, moderate.
G1334: To relate in full, describe, narrate. From dia and hegeomai; to relate fully.
G4918: To press on all sides, crowd upon. From sun and thlibo; to compress, i.e. Crowd on all sides.
G1159: To spend, bear expense, waste, squander. From dapane; to expend, i.e. to incur cost, or to waste.
G5141: To tremble, be afraid. Strengthened from a primary treo; to |tremble| or fear.
G4870: To accompany, follow together with. From sun and akoloutheo; to accompany.
G214: From alale; to vociferate, i.e. to wail; figuratively, to clang.
G4773: Akin to, related; subst: fellow countryman, kinsman. From sun and genos; a relative; by extension, a fellow countryman.
G5265: From hupo and deo; to bind under one's feet, i.e. Put on shoes or sandals.
G5522: Earth, soil, dust. From the base of cheimon; a heap, i.e. Rubbish; loose dirt.
G1758: From en and echo; to hold in or upon, i.e. Ensnare; by implication, to keep a grudge.
G639: From a compound of a and the base of poreuomai; to have no way out, i.e. Be at a loss.
G2234: Gladly, pleasantly, with pleasure. Adverb from a derivative of the base of hedone; sweetly, i.e. with pleasure.
G2121: Opportune, timely, suitable; perhaps sometimes: holiday, festival. From eu and kairos; well-timed, i.e. Opportune.
G3175: A great one, a lord; a courtier, satrap, nobleman. Plural from megistos; grandees.
G5506: A commander of a thousand men, a military tribune. From chilioi and archo; the commander of a thousand soldiers
G2255: Half. Neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to hama and meaning semi-; half.
G4710: (a) speed, haste, (b) diligence, earnestness, enthusiasm. From speudo; |speed|, i.e. despatch, eagerness, earnestness.
G1824: Immediately, instantly, at once. From ek and the genitive case singular feminine of autos; from that hour, i.e. Instantly.
G114: From a compound of a and a derivative of tithemi; to set aside, i.e. to disesteem, neutralize or violate.
G4688: A body-guardsman; an executioner. Of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. Military scout (by extension) life-guardsman).
G2119: From eukairos; to have good time, i.e. Opportunity or leisure.
G4936: To run (rush) together, run with. From sun and trecho; to rush together or headlong.
G4849: A drinking party, festive company. Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of sumpino; a drinking-party, i.e. a room of guests.
G4237: A company formed into divisions (like garden-beds). Perhaps from prason; a garden plot, i.e. a row.
G2622: To break in pieces, break up. From kata and klao; to break down, i.e. Divide.
G1643: (a) trans: I drive (on), propel, (b) intrans: I row. A prolonged form of a primary verb of uncertain affinity; to push.
G4456: To harden, render callous, petrify. Apparently from poros; to petrify, i.e. to indurate.
G4358: I anchor at a place. From pros and a derivative of the same as horme (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. land at.
G4063: To run around. From peri and trecho; to run around, i.e. Traverse.
G4064: To carry around; pass: To be driven to and fro. From peri and phero; to convey around, i.e. Transport hither and thither.
G5473: A bronze vessel, brazen utensil. Diminutive from chalkos; a copper dish.
G4435: The fist. From a primary pux; the clenched hand, i.e. with the fist.
G3582: As if from xeo (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel, i.e., a measure for liquids or solids.
G4124: Covetousness, avarice, aggression, desire for advantage. From pleonektes; avarice, i.e. fraudulency, extortion.
G877: Want of sense, foolishness, impiety, wickedness. From aphron; senselessness, i.e. egotism; recklessness.
G2990: A prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; to lie hid; often used adverbially, unwittingly.
G4949: Feminine of a compound of Suros and the same as Phoinike; a Syro-phoenician woman, i.e. A female native of Phoenicia in Syria.
G3424: One speaking with difficulty, a stammerer. From mogis and laleo; hardly talking, i.e. Dumb.
G216: Unable to speak or articulate; speechless. Mute.
G4727: To groan, expressing grief, anger, or desire. From stenos; to make in straits, i.e. to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly.
G2188: (Aramaic, meaning) be opened up. Of Chaldee origin; be opened!
G1272: To open fully. From dia and anoigo; to open thoroughly, literally or figuratively.
G1199: Or desmos des-mos' neuter and masculine respectively from deo; a band, i.e. Ligament or shackle; figuratively, an impediment or disability.
G1148: Dalmanutha, a town or village near Magdala. Probably of Chaldee origin; Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine.
G389: To groan or sigh deeply. From ana and stenazo; to sigh deeply.
G1627: To bring out, carry out, sometimes out of the city for burial; I bring forth, bear, produce. From ek and phero; to bear out.
G5081: Clearly, distinctly, plainly. Adverb from a compound of a derivative of telos and auge; in a far-shining manner, i.e. Plainly.
G3954: From pas and a derivative of rheo; all out-spokenness, i.e. Frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance.
G4744: To shine, glisten, flash, be radiant. Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. Flash intensely.
G1102: A fuller, cloth-dresser. By variation for a derivative from knapto; a cloth-dresser.
G1630: Greatly terrified, horrified. From ek and phobos; frightened out of one's wits: sore afraid, exceedingly fear.
G1568: To be greatly astonished, be awe-struck. From ekthambos; to astonish utterly.
