G255: Profitless, unprofitable, ruinous, detrimental. Gainless, i.e. pernicious.
G1383: A test, trial, what is genuine. Neuter of a presumed derivative of dokime; a testing; by implication, trustworthiness.
G1503: To be like, resemble. Apparently a primary verb; to resemble.
G416: To be blown with the wind (referring to the gentler motions of the air). From anemos; to toss with the wind.
G4494: To toss to and fro, fan, blow. From a derivative of rhipto; to breeze up, i.e. to agitate.
G1374: (lit: of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering. From dis and psuche; two-spirited, i.e. Vacillating.
G182: Unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic. Inconstant.
G438: Bloom, possibly a reference to the bright flowers, such as poppies (among the grass). A primary word; a blossom.
G2143: Beauty, gracefulness, comeliness. From a compound of eu and prepo; good suitableness, i.e. Gracefulness.
G3133: Pass: I die, wither (like the grass). Of uncertain affinity; to extinguish, i.e. to pass away.
G551: Untried, inexperienced, untempted, incapable of being tempted. Untried, i.e. Not temptable.
G1828: From ek and helkuo; to drag forth, i.e. to entice.
G1185: To allure, entice (by a bait). From the base of dolos; to entrap, i.e. delude.
G616: From apo and the base of kuma; to breed forth, i.e. to generate.
G3883: A change, variation, mutation. From a compound of para and allasso; transmutation, i.e. fickleness: variableness.
G5157: A turning, change, mutation. From an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn, i.e. Revolution.
G644: From a compound of apo and a derivative of skia; a shading off, i.e. Obscuration.
G5036: Quick, swift, speedy, ready, prompt. Of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. prompt or ready.
G1721: Inborn, ingrown, congenital, natural, rooted, implanted. From en and a derivative of phuo; implanted.
G1953: Forgetfulness, oblivion. From a derivative of epilanthanomai; negligence.
G4162: A doing, making, performance. From poieo; action, i.e. Performance.
G2357: Probably from the base of throeo; ceremonious in worship, i.e. Pious.
G5468: To bridle, curb, restrain, sway. From a compound of chalinos and the reduplicated form of ago; to be a bit-leader, i.e. To curb.
G5554: Adorned with a gold ring. From chrusos and daktulios; gold-ringed, i.e. Wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry.
G4508: Filthy, defiled, dirty. From rhupos; dirty, i.e. cheap or shabby; morally, wicked.
G4380: To favor specially, show partiality. From prosopoleptes; to favor an individual, i.e. Show partiality.
G2184: For the day, daily, necessary for every day. From epi and hemera; for a day, i.e. Diurnal.
G5425: To shudder, shiver, tremble. Apparently a primary verb; to |bristle| or chill, i.e. Shudder.
G1724: Marine, living in the sea. From en and hals; in the sea, i.e. Marine.
G5469: A bridle, bit. From chalao; a curb or head-stall.
G3329: From meta and harmozo; to lead over, i.e. Transfer.
G3166: To boast, be arrogant, vaunt. From a compound of megas and aucheo; to talk big, i.e. Be grandiloquent.
G5164: A wheel, course. From trecho; a wheel, i.e. a circuit of physical effects.
G4695: To defile, spot, stain, soil. From spilos; to stain or soil.
G5394: To inflame, fire with passion, set on fire, burn up. From phlox; to cause a blaze, i.e. Ignite.
G2287: Death-bringing, deadly. From thanatos and phero; death-bearing, i.e. Fatal.
G3669: Making like, likeness, resemblance. From homoioo; assimilation, i.e. Resemblance.
G5534: It is necessary, proper, fitting. Third person singular of the same as chraomai or chrao used impersonally; it needs be.
G1032: To cause to gush forth, send forth. A primary verb; to swell out, i.e. to gush.
G252: Salty, saltine, bitter. From hals; briny.
G2138: Compliant, ready to obey. From eu and peitho; good for persuasion, i.e. complaint.
G87: Without uncertainty, unambiguous, undivided, whole-hearted. Properly, undistinguished, i.e. impartial.
G5003: To endure severe hardship, be harassed, complain. From talaiporos; to be wretched, i.e. Realize one's own misery.
G2726: From a compound of kata and perhaps a derivative of the base of phaino; demureness, i.e. sadness.
G2635: To speak evil of, rail at, slander. From katalalos; to be a traducer, i.e. To slander.
G1710: From en and poreuomai; to travel in, i.e. to trade.
G3649: To howl, lament loudly, cry aloud, bewail. A reduplicated primary verb; to |howl| or |halloo|, i.e. Shriek.
G4595: To cause to rot, make corrupt. Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. perish.
G2728: To rust; pass: To be rusted, tarnished. From kata and a derivative of ios; to rust down, i.e. Corrode.
G4406: Dawning, early. From proi; dawning, i.e. autumnal.
G270: To mow, reap, collect. From hama; properly, to collect, i.e. reap.
G5171: To live a luxurious life, live self-indulgently. From truphe; to indulge in luxury.
G3797: Late, latter. From opse; later, i.e. Vernal.
G2552: Experience of evil, suffering, distress, affliction, perseverance. From a compound of hemiorion and pathos; hardship.
G2492: (Hebrew), Job, the hero of the book of that name in the Old Testament. Of Hebrew origin; Job, a patriarch.
G4184: Very compassionate, of great mercy. From polus and splagchnon; extremely compassionate.
G313: To beget again, beget into a new life. From ana and gennao; to beget or bear.
G1830: To search diligently, I examine carefully (minutely). From ek and ereunao; to explore.
G4303: To predict, testify or protest beforehand. From pro and marturomai; to be a witness in advance i.e. Predict.
G5049: Perfectly, completely, without wavering. Adverb from teleios; completely, i.e. without wavering.
G97: Unadulterated, pure, guileless. Undeceitful, i.e. unadulterated.
G3970: Handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited. From pater and a derivative of paradidomi; traditionary.
G738: Newly begotten, newly born. From arti and gennetos; just born, i.e. a young convert.
G2406: The act or office of priesthood. From hierateuo; the priestly fraternity, i.e. Sacerdotal order.
G1804: To announce publicly, proclaim. From ek and the base of aggelos; to publish, i.e. Celebrate.
G2555: Doing evil; subst: an evil-doer. From kakos and poieo; a bad-doer;, a criminal.
G2029: To be an eyewitness of, behold, look upon. From epi and a derivative of optanomai; to inspect, i.e. Watch.
G17: A doer of that which is good. From agathos and poieo; a well-doer, i.e. Virtuous.
G1942: A covering, cloak, veil, pretext. From epikalupto; a covering, i.e. pretext.
G2811: Glory, fame, praise; rumor, report, credit. From a shorter form of kaleo; renown.
G5277: To leave behind. A prolonged form for hupoleipo; to leave behind, i.e. Bequeath.
G5261: A writing-copy, an example, pattern. From a compound of hupo and grapho; an underwriting, i.e. Copy for imitation.
G486: To abuse in return, give abuse for abuse. From anti and loidoreo; to rail in reply.
G581: To be away, be removed from, depart life, die. Past participle of a compound of apo and ginomai; absent, i.e. Deceased.
G3468: A bruise, stripe, left on the body by scourging. From molos and probably ops; a mole or blow-mark.
G4025: A putting around or on (as of ornaments). From peritithemi; a putting all around, i.e. Decorating oneself with.
G4924: To dwell with, live in wedlock with. From sun and oikeo; to reside together.
G632: To assign, apportion, render (as due). From apo and the base of nomos; to apportion, i.e. Bestow.
G3675: Of one mind (intent, purpose), like-minded. From the base of homou and phren; like-minded, i.e. Harmonious.
G4835: Sympathizing, compassionate. From sumpascho; having a fellow-feeling, i.e. mutually commiserative.
G5361: Loving like a brother, loving one's brethren. From philos and adephos; fond of brethren, i.e. Fraternal.
G1906: Inquiry, request, appeal, demand; a profession, pledge. From eperotao; an inquiry.
G3695: To make ready, arm, equip. From hoplon; to equip (middle voice and figuratively).
G1954: Remaining, that is left over, still left. From epi and loipoy; left over, i.e. Remaining.
G3632: Drunkenness, debauchery. From oinos and a form of the base of phluaros; an overflow of wine, i.e. Vinolency.
G4224: A drinking, carousing. From the alternate of pino; a drinking-bout or carousal.
G401: Outpouring, excess, overflow, a pouring out. From a comparative of ana and cheo; properly, effusion, i.e. license.
G1618: Intent, constant, strenuous, intense; met: earnest, zealous. From ekteino; intent.
G244: From allotrios and episkopos; overseeing others' affairs, i.e. A meddler.
G750: The chief shepherd. From arche and poimen; a head shepherd.
G16: The doing of that which is good, well-doing. From agathopoios; well-doing, i.e. Virtue.
G4850: A fellow elder. From sun and presbuteros; a co-presbyter.
G317: By way of compulsion, unwillingly, by force, necessarily. Adverb from a derivative of anagkazo; compulsorily.
G262: Unfading, fadeless, enduring. From amarantos; |amaranthine|, i.e. fadeless.
G1463: To clothe oneself (originally: To tie round in a knot).
G2900: Strong, powerful, mighty. From kratos; powerful.
G5612: To roar, howl, as a beast. Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to |roar|.
G4599: To strengthen. From sthenos; to strengthen, i.e. confirm.
G1957: To testify earnestly, bear witness to. From epi and martureo; to attest further, i.e. Corroborate.
G4899: Fellow-elect, fellow-chosen. From a compound of sun and eklegomai; chosen in company with, i.e. Co-elect.
G2472: Equally privileged, equal in honor. From isos and time; of equal value or honor.
G1862: A promise. From epaggello; a self-committal.
G668: To flee from, escape. From apo and pheugo; to escape.
G3923: From para and eisphero; to bear in alongside, i.e. Introduce simultaneously.
G3467: To be short-sighted, blink, see dimly. From a compound of the base of musterion and ops; to shut the eyes, i.e. Blink.
G1811: To follow after, imitate. From ek and akoloutheo; to follow out, i.e. to imitate, obey, yield to.
G2030: An eyewitness, spectator, looker-on. From epi and a presumed derivative of optanomai; a looker-on.
G3169: Magnificent, superb, transcendent, majestic. From megas and prepo; befitting greatness or magnificence.
G5107: Of this kind, such, such as follows. (including the other inflections); from a derivative of toi and de; such-like then, i.e. So great.
G850: From auchmos; properly, dirty, i.e. obscure.
G1306: To shine through, dawn (of the light coming through the shadows). From dia and augazo; to glimmer through, i.e. Break.
G5459: (lit: light-bearing), radiant, the morning-star. From phos and phero; light-bearing, i.e., the morning-star.
G1955: Solution, explanation, interpretation; release. From epiluo; explanation, i.e. Application.
G5572: From pseudes and didaskalos; a spurious teacher, i.e. Propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine.
G3919: To bring in secretly, be at hand. From para and eisago; to lead in aside, i.e. Introduce surreptitiously.
G4112: Formed, molded; fig: feigned, made up, counterfeit. From plasso; moulded, i.e. artificial or fictitious.
G691: To linger, delay, be idle. From argos; to be idle, i.e. to delay.
G5020: To thrust down to Tartarus or Gehenna. From Tartaros; to incarcerate in eternal torment.
G3394: The act of pollution, defilement. From miaino; contamination.
G5077: To reduce to ashes, consume, destroy. From tephra; to incinerate, i.e. Consume.
G1460: To dwell in, among. From en and katoikeo; to settle down in a place, i.e. Reside.
G259: Capture, capturing. From a collateral form of haireomai; capture, be taken.
G3470: A blemish, disgrace; blame. Perhaps from memphomai; a flaw or blot, i.e. disgraceful person.
G1792: To revel (in), live luxuriously, riot. From en and truphao; to revel in.
G180: Not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up). Unrefraining.
G793: (lit: unpropped), unsteady, unstable, unsettled. Unfixed, i.e. vacillating.
G903: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament. Of Hebrew origin; Balaam, a Mesopotamian.
G1007: Bosor, father of Balaam. Of Hebrew origin; Bosor, a Moabite.
G1649: Rebuke, reproof, refutation. From elegcho; refutation, i.e. Reproof.
G3913: Madness, folly. From paraphroneo; insanity, i.e. Foolhardiness.
G3892: A transgression, violation of law. From the same as paranomeo; transgression: iniquity.
G5246: Immoderate, boastful, excessive, pompous. From huper and ogkos; bulging over, i.e. insolent.
G1829: Vomit. From a comparative of ek and a presumed erao; vomit, i.e. Food disgorged.
G2626: To flood over, overwhelm, inundate. From kata and the base of kludon; to dash down, i.e. to deluge.
G4500: With a great noise, with a rushing sound. Adverb from a derivative of rhoizos; whizzingly, i.e. With a crash.
G2741: To burn with great heat. From kausis; to set on fire.
G5080: To make liquid; pass: I melt (away). Apparently a primary verb; to liquefy.
G1425: Hard to understand. From dus- and a derivative of noieo; difficult of perception.
G4761: From a derivative of strepho; to wrench, i.e., to torture, but only figuratively, to pervert.
G2434: A propitiation (of an angry god), atoning sacrifice. Atonement, i.e. an expiator.
G4969: To slay, kill by violence, slaughter, wound mortally. A primary verb; to butcher or to slaughter, or, to maim.
G3529: Victory, a victorious principle. Apparently a primary word; conquest, i.e. the means of success.
G5489: Papyrus, paper. From the same as charax; a sheet of writing-material.
G1361: Diotrephes. From the alternate of Zeus and trepho; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity.
G5383: From a compound of philos and protos; to be fond of being first, i.e. Ambitious of distinction.
G1926: To accept, admit, welcome. From epi and dechomai; to admit (figuratively) teacher.
G5396: From phluaros; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. to berate idly or mischievously.
G1864: To contend earnestly for. From epi and agonizomai; to struggle for.
G3921: To enter secretly, come in by stealth. From para and a compound of eis and duno; to settle in alongside, i.e. Lodge stealthily.
G1608: To be guilty of fornication. From ek and porneuo; to be utterly unchaste.
G5254: To submit to, undergo, suffer. From hupo and echo; to hold oneself under, i.e. Endure with patience.
G4694: A hidden rock; fig: a flaw, stigma. Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea.
G5352: Autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected. From derivative of phthino and opora; autumnal.
G1113: A murmurer, grumbler. From gogguzo; a grumbler.
G764: To be ungodly, act profanely. From asebes; to be impious or wicked.
G3202: From a presumed derivative of memphomai and moira; blaming fate, i.e. Querulous.
G592: To make a logical distinction, make an invidious distinction. From apo and a compound of Alexandros and horizo; to disjoin.
G679: Without stumbling or falling, sure-footed. Not stumbling, i.e. without sin.
G5598: Omega, the last letter of the Greek alphabet. The last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. the finality.
G3963: Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean.
G4667: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia. The same as smurna; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor.
G4010: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia. From purgos; fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor.
G4554: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia. Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor.
G5359: Philadelphia, a city of the Roman province Asia. From Philadelphos, a king of Pergamos; Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor.
G4158: Reaching to the feet (of a garment). From pous and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress reaching the ankles.
G5474: Neuter of a compound of chalkos and libanos; burnished copper, an alloy of copper and silver having a brilliant lustre.
G3531: A Nicolaitan, possibly a follower of Nicolaus (a heretic at Ephesus). From Nikolaos; a Nicolaite, i.e. Adherent of Nicolaus.
G493: Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum. Contracted for a compound of anti and a derivative of pater; Antipas, a Christian.
G904: Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab. Of Hebrew origin; Balak, a Moabite.
G3510: A kidney (as a general emotional center), the reins. Of uncertain affinity; a kidney, i.e. the inmost mind.
G2764: Of clay, made by a potter, earthen. From keramos; made of clay, i.e. Earthen.
G4407: Belonging to the morning, early. From proi; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. Matutinal.
G5513: Warm, tepid; of persons: lukewarm. From chlio; tepid.
G1692: To vomit forth. Of uncertain affinity; to vomit.
G2854: Eye-salve. Neuter of a presumed derivative of kollura; properly, a poultice, i.e. a plaster.
G4556: Carnelian, a precious stone. Properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian, i.e. the gem so called.
G4664: Made of emerald, emerald-green. From smaragdos; consisting of emerald.
G2943: In a circle round, round about. Adverb from the same as kukloi; from the circle, i.e. All around.
G5193: Glassy, made of glass, transparent. From hualos; glassy, i.e. Transparent.
G4072: To fly. Or prolongation petaomai, or contracted ptaomai middle voice of a primary verb; to fly.
G2696: To seal up, secure with a seal. From kata and sphragizo; to seal closely.
G5518: A Greek dry measure, equivalent to 1.92 pints. Of uncertain derivation; a choenix or certain dry measure.
G4502: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe. Of Hebrew origin; Ruben, an Israelite.
G1045: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Of Hebrew origin; Gad, a tribe of Israelites.
G3031: A censer. From libanos; frankincense, i.e. a censer for burning it.
G894: Wormwood. Of uncertain derivation; wormwood (figuratively) calamity).
G4141: To strike, smite. Apparently another form of plasso; to pound, i.e. to inflict with.
G3321: Mid-heaven, the middle of heaven, the zenith. From a presumed compound of mesos and ouranos; mid-sky.
G3: Abaddon, Destroyer (i.e. Destroying Angel) or place of destruction (personified). Of Hebrew origin; a destroying angel.
G623: Apollyon, The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebrew: Abaddon. Active participle of apollumi; a destroyer.
G2166: The Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria. Of foreign origin; Euphrates, a river of Asia.
G2461: Cavalry. Neuter of a derivative of hippos; the cavalry force.
G5191: Dark purple or blue, of the color of hyacinth. From huakinthos; |hyacinthine| or |jacinthine|, i.e. Deep blue.
G2306: Of brimstone, sulfurous. From theion and eidos; sulphur-like, i.e. Sulphurous.
G3455: To bellow, roar. From a presumed derivative of muzo; to bellow.
G1404: A dragon or huge serpent; met: Satan. Probably from an alternate form of derkomai; a fabulous kind of serpent.
G1238: A head-wreath, crown, diadem. From a compound of dia and deo; a |diadem|.
G4216: Carried away by a stream. From potamos and a derivative of phoreo; river-borne, i.e. Overwhelmed by a stream.
G3917: A leopard, panther. Feminine of pardos; a leopard.
G715: A bear. Probably from arkeo; a bear.
G2790: From kithara and a derivative of the same as oide; a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. Harpist.
G2767: To mix, mingle, pour out for drinking. Prolonged form of a more primary kerao ker-ah'-o; to mingle, i.e. to pour out.
G1009: A cluster (bunch) of grapes. Of uncertain derivation; a bunch.
G187: To reach maturity, become ripe, am in full vigor. From the same as akmen; to make a point, i.e. mature.
G3145: To bite, gnaw, chew. From a primary masso; to chew.
G717: Armageddon. Of Hebrew origin; Armageddon, a symbolic name.
G5006: A talent in weight. From talanton; talent-like in weight.
G5558: To gild, adorn with gold. From chrusos; to gild, i.e. Bespangle with golden ornaments.
G4764: Wantonness, luxury. Akin to stereos; a |straining|, |strenuousness| or |strength|, i.e. luxury.
G1363: To double, render back double. From diplous; to render two-fold.
G4763: To live luxuriously, revel, riot. From a presumed derivative of strenos; to be luxurious.
G2792: (a Semitic word) cinnamon. Of foreign origin; cinnamon.
G2367: Of the sandarach (so-called citron) tree. From a derivative of thuo; made of citron-wood.
G1661: Made of ivory, subst: ivory. From elephas; elephantine, i.e. composed of ivory.
G4585: The finest wheaten flour. Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour.
G3703: Autumn, autumnal fruits. Apparently from the base of opse and hora; properly, even-tide of the season, i.e. ripe fruit.
G5094: Preciousness, costliness, worth. From timios; expensiveness, i.e. magnificence.
G3731: A rushing on, impulse, violence. From horme; an attack, i.e. precipitancy.
G3451: Skilled in music; subst: a musician, singer. From Mousa; |musical|, i.e. a minstrel.
G239: Hallelujah, Praise the Lord. Of Hebrew origin; praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation.
G3382: The thigh. Perhaps a primary word; a thigh.
G3990: To behead (with an axe). From a derivative of plesso; to chop off, i.e. Truncate.
G1136: Of Hebrew origin; Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist.
G3098: Of Hebrew origin; Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. an Antichristian party.
G2929: To be clear as crystal, brilliant like crystal. From krustallos; to make ice.
G5068: Square, four-cornered. From tessares and gonia; four-cornered, i.e. Square.
G1739: From a compound of en and a derivative of the base of demos; a housing in, i.e. Structure.
G5194: Glass, crystal, clear transparent stone. Perhaps from the same as huetos; glass.
G5472: Chalcedony, a small stone of various colors. From chalkos and perhaps eidos; copper-like, i.e. |chalcedony|.
G4665: An emerald. Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called.
G4557: From the base of sardios and onux; a |sardonyx|, i.e. The gem so called.
G5555: A topaz, a gem with a bright yellow color. From chrusos and lithos; gold-stone, i.e. A yellow gem.
G969: A beryl, a precious stone of various colors, the best known being sea-green. Of uncertain derivation; a |beryl|.
G5116: Topaz. Neuter of a presumed derivative of topazos; a gem, probably the chrysolite.
G5556: A chrysoprase, gem of a golden-greenish color. From chrusos and prason; a greenish-yellow gem.
G5192: The |hyacinth| or |jacinth|, i.e. Some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon.
G2652: A curse, an accursed thing. From kata and anathema; an imprecation.
G4510: To be filthy; hence (morally): To be stained with sin. From rhupos; to soil, i.e. to become dirty.
